title: Serialize verified performance profiles to Git with deferred-refresh policy and telemetry snapshots
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Goal: produce an auditable, git-serializable artifact for each Redwood-verified model performance profile (latency, throughput, cost) and introduce a deferred-refresh policy that reduces churn for stable profiles while ensuring stale profiles get revalidated on demand. This ticket captures the PM definition, acceptance criteria, rollout constraints, and telemetry snapshot contract to be serialized alongside profiles.
background: We've observed frequent small updates to performance profiles during model minor-version churn that cause downstream noise for Dedicated and Private customers who pin profiles. Existing 'immediate publish' behavior leads to alert fatigue in platform sync jobs and unnecessary canaries for low-impact measurement changes. Engineering has proposed a git-serialized manifest and a deferred refresh policy where non-critical metric drifts are batched and validated on a schedule unless a breaking threshold is crossed.
success_criteria: Verified profile manifests are written as single-file JSON/YAML to the profiles git repo with immutable SHA references
Deferred-refresh policy implemented: non-breaking metric deltas <5% are queued and revalidated during nightly refresh window
Telemetry snapshot (compact cost/latency/throughput per canonical workload) is included in manifest and parsed by Console dashboards
Rolling canary that reads git-backed manifests demonstrates zero customer-facing regression in Dedicated region alpha customers during a 2-week trial
Operational playbook updated with rollback steps and indicators for forced immediate refresh
acceptance_criteria: Create PR template for profile serialization that validates schema and signs the manifest (link: https://github.com/redwood/profiles/pulls)
Build a lightweight linter that runs in CI and blocks malformed manifests
Implement deferred-refresh controller with abort-on-threshold and a public status endpoint (internal-only)
Console reads telemetry snapshot from git and shows cost-per-1k-tokens and p50/p95 latency in profile view
Document migration for existing pinned profiles and provide a one-click opt-in for customers to enable deferred-refresh
notes: Trade-offs: immediate publish preserves freshness but increases churn; deferred-refresh reduces churn but requires clear thresholds and emergency refresh paths
Security: manifests are public within our org git and must be signed. KMS signing will be handled by ENG-89214
Telemetry contract: compact snapshot limited to <= 2KB per profile to prevent repo bloat
Operational hooks: add 'force_refresh' label on PRs and a /refresh API endpoint for emergency revalidation
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize manifest schema with ENG and DX teams. Reference: confluence/redwood/model-profiles/schema-draft
Week 2: Implement serializer in onboarding pipeline and add CI linter. Create initial PRs to profiles repo
Week 3: Implement deferred-refresh controller and webhook that schedules nightly revalidations
Week 4: Wire Console to consume snapshot fields and surface cost/latency summary
Week 5: Run two-week canary with Dedicated alpha customers, gather feedback, iterate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Repo becomes source of truth inconsistency. Mitigation: enforce single-writer pipeline and CI checks; periodic reconciliation job
Risk: Deferred-refresh masks real regressions. Mitigation: aggressive thresholds for rollback and 'drift alarms' tied to evals
Risk: Customers confused by delayed profile updates. Mitigation: add 'last_validated' timestamp and 'staleness' badge in Console
qa_plan: Unit tests for serializer and linter, coverage >90%
Integration tests: onboard synthetic model and assert manifest content is correct
Staging canary: 5 Dedicated alpha customers subscribe to git-backed profiles and report mismatches
Chaos test: simulate runtime kernel regression and assert forced immediate refresh path triggers
rollout_strategy: Start with internal profiles and Dedicated alpha group (2 tenants). If stable after 2 weeks, expand to Beta (10 tenants) and then default for new onboardings. Provide opt-out for existing pinned customers and migration guide.
observability_requirements: Emit 'profile_published' and 'profile_deferred' events to telemetry with profile_sha
Dashboard: publish rate, deferred queue length, average time-to-refresh, canary failure rate
Alert: deferred queue >1000 items for >24h or forced_refresh failures >5% in 1h
